Title: Hung Parliament threatens Mindanao's autonomy progress
Article:
Twelve years after the 2014 Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro (CAB) between the Philippine government and the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) —which was facilitated by Malaysia —the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) held its first parliamentary election on Sept 14.
The election, postponed four times since it was first scheduled for 2022, was relatively peaceful, with turnout exceeding 80 per cent of eligible voters.
Unfortunately, it produced a hung Parliament, with the two largest parties winning 31 and 30 seats respectively.
Either the Manila-backed Bangsamoro Federalist Party or the MILF-backed United Bangsamoro Justice Party will need to cobble together a coalition with minor parties to form the new BARMM government by month's end.
That the election only took place after four false starts exposes the glacial pace the BARMM interim appointed government took in bringing about a sense of normalcy after previous decades of political and clan rivalries and armed struggles.
It can be argued that the past dozen years were mostly wasted; the decommissioning of MILF combatants remains incomplete, for any number of reasons.
The most significant of these is probably the lack of economic incentives for armed insurgents to return peacefully to productive civilian lives.
Such uncompleted tasks will now fall on the newly elected Parliament and regional government to address.
It remains to be seen if the fractured politics that emerged from the election will be any better at meeting the considerable challenges confronting BARMM.
It was never intended to be this way.
The CAB and its enabling Organic Law provided for a parliamentary system, with the BARMM chief minister to be elected by Parliament rather than a directly elected governor functioning alongside a separately elected legislature, as happens elsewhere in the Philippines.
Such a system of government for BARMM was chosen in an indirect nod to the parliamentary system adopted in Malaysia.
It was felt that our governance system produces governments that are more effective and more accountable.
This may be true only if governments elected possess unambiguous majorities.
Such majorities in Malaysia have often been achieved through coalitions nationally and at state level.
Which is why the first Bangsamoro parliamentary election provides some glimmer of hope that a sturdy and stable coalition government will follow.
There has to be enough parliamentary leaders elected who can rise above either sectoral or political cleavages to tackle all the formidable BARMM challenges.
The priorities are obvious: attaining real and durable peace through disarming of armed groups so that a focus can be swiftly shifted towards the regional economy.
Unless the young and restless population of BARMM can see and feel the promise of peace through expanded economic opportunities, discord and continued political unrest will further disenchant them.
The promise and hopes that CAB envisions for BARMM now rest with its freshly elected Parliament.
It has to also prove that regional political autonomy does not end up as just little more than an empty slogan.
The writer views developments in the nation, region and the wider world from his vantage point in Kuching
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Denmark hails 'binding' Greenland deal with Trump
Article:
COPENHAGEN: Denmark on Saturday hailed a "binding" deal announced by US President Donald Trump to give Washington "permanent control" over Greenland's security and bar Russian and Chinese bases from the Arctic territory.
Since returning to the White House in January 2025, Trump has repeatedly insisted that Washington needed to control Greenland for strategic reasons, alarming NATO ally Denmark and sparking fierce pushback from the alliance.
Denmark and Greenland – an autonomous Danish territory – both hailed the deal and said they would sign it on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York next week.
Danish Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen said Saturday the potential signing meant "next week could be a good week."
"A long period of uncertainty will hopefully be replaced by a binding agreement that strengthens security in the Arctic and North Atlantic," the foreign minister said in a social media post.
The deal respected Denmark's "red lines" and was "important" in light of a changed security situation, he said.
'Permanent control' -
While the terms are still unclear, Denmark maintains that its sovereignty remains intact.
Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said the agreement "recognises the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Kingdom and the Greenlandic people's right to self-determination."
Trump meanwhile hailed it as an "'Infinite Life' Agreement, there is no end!" and said Washington would immediately start building up a large military presence in the territory.
"From now on, no US adversary can EVER have a base in Greenland, have a military presence in Greenland, or make sensitive investments in Greenland, without our express written approval."
While Trump presented the deal as a major triumph, Danish commentators said he had not really gained anything, noting that Washington was already able to ramp up its military presence on the island provided it informs Denmark and Greenland in advance, under a 1951 defence pact updated in 2004.
"Shhh. Don't tell Trump that it's the Kingdom of Denmark that has prevailed," US correspondent Jacob Heinel Jensen wrote in the Danish newspaper Berlingske on Saturday.
"Donald Trump gets out of it that he can appear as a winner. He has been a good businessman who has pushed Denmark and Greenland into something new," Marc Jacobsen, a researcher at the Royal Danish Defence College, told AFP.
Trump has repeatedly warned of Russia and China trying to establish a foothold in Greenland as a strategic battle for supremacy in a warming Arctic unfolds, and the State Department left no doubt that they would not be allowed to do so.
"This agreement guarantees that China and Russia cannot have a base in Greenland, they cannot send troops to Greenland, and the necessary mechanisms are in place to prevent investment in sensitive sectors," a State Department official said.
Frederiksen said Friday she was "pleased that there is a prospect of a good agreement for Greenland, the Kingdom of Denmark and the United States," adding that it was "good for NATO and Europe."
Greenland Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen said the deal with the United States "strengthens" the territory's security.
NATO tensions -
Trump gave no details about how the deal would work.
But several media outlets have reported that the United States wants to open three new military bases in southern Greenland, in addition to the Pituffik base it already has in the north of the territory.
At the height of the crisis, Trump would not rule out using force to seize the territory of 57,000 inhabitants, sowing anxiety within the EU and NATO.
Since then, tensions have cooled somewhat, and in an apparent move to assuage Trump, NATO launched a new mission to bolster security in the Arctic.
Danes strolling in Copenhagen on Saturday were cautiously optimistic about the deal.
"I hope this is a definitive and sound deal once the details are known but I wouldn't be surprised if we have to take a step back again and then hopefully two steps forward," Soren, a 52-year-old IT executive, told AFP.
He feared the announcement was "maybe a little bit premature."
Katrine Rasmussen, a 47-year-old lawyer, said she hoped the agreement would be the last word.
"It would be nice if we could end these discussions, at least that would be a good outcome, so we can move on."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NST Leader: What led to Tasik Bera land grab?
Article:
Land encroachment is as ancient as land ownership, going back thousands of years. About 2,000 years ago, Rome established rights over land ownership and strict property boundaries, penalising accidental or deliberate construction of walls over a neighbour's boundary.
In the 11th century, post-Norman conquest, medieval England pioneered the Domesday Book, a 1086 tool to bar encroachment by logging.
In the United States, this historical dispute still simmers: the 19th century Wild West land grab to open up millions of hectares of Indigenous land for white and immigrant settlers.
Ancient encroachment changed in the 1960s after modern laws, strict suburban boundaries and precise surveying were institutionalised to enable litigation over disputed ownership.
In Malaysia, the problem pales in scale, but is still troublesome: concessionaires procure state contracts to log plots, only to discover that the trees had long been felled and cleared.
But this timber theft pales in comparison to the recently discovered encroachment on the Tasek Bera Permanent Forest Reserve.
One, the unbelievable size of encroachment: 7,000ha, the equivalent of almost 10,000 football fields.
Two, encroachers did not steal and run. Instead, they cleared the forest reserve and grew oil palm, rubber and cash crops.
Syndicates allegedly manipulated the Orang Asli under the pretext that the areas are "customary land" and Orang Asli "roaming" areas.
How did this operation go undetected? What is galling is that Tasek Bera is one of Malaysia's seven sites ratified under the Ramsar Convention on Wetlands, covering 5.2 million hectares of wetland ecosystems.
Since ratifying the convention in 1994, Malaysia designated significant areas for monitoring and enforcement.
There seems to be two versions of the encroachment story. The first: the Semelais, currently facing eviction, insist that their families have made legitimate livelihoods from these plantations for over five decades.
The second: the Pahang State Enforcement Unit's surveillance drones detected unlicensed swaths of oil palm and rubber trees yielding market-ready crops.
Drone footage suggests that tracts were scorched and cleared only recently, which triggered the state's eviction warnings in June and the current crackdown.
Syndicate masterminds would have scarpered by now, already harvesting tonnes of crops and making handsome profits.
By how much is still unclear. The bigger concern: since Tasik Bera is under intraagency surveillance, did the encroachment stem from incompetence, neglect or corruption? The authorities have to explain how the system failed to detect, prevent and stop this.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: One killed, six seriously injured in three-vehicle crash in Kota Tinggi
Article:
KOTA TINGGI: A man was killed and six others seriously injured in a three-vehicle crash at KM66.6 of the Senai-Desaru Expressway here today.
Kota Tinggi district police chief Superintendent Yusof Othman said the deceased, Chua Bing Xuan, 26, was a passenger in a Perodua Myvi.
He said police received information from members of the public about the crash at 11.50am.
"The crash involved a Perodua Myvi driven by a 21-year-old man with four passengers, a Proton Exora driven by a 56-year-old man with one passenger, and a Mazda CX-30 driven by a 30-year-old man.
"The driver and all passengers of the Perodua Myvi and Proton Exora were seriously injured and taken to Sultan Ismail Hospital (HSI) in Johor Baru, Pasir Gudang Hospital (HPG) and Kota Tinggi Hospital (HKT) for treatment," he said in a statement today.
Yusof said the crash was believed to have occurred when the Perodua Myvi overtook another vehicle before colliding with the Proton Exora travelling in the opposite direction.
"The Mazda CX-30 then crashed into the rear of the Proton Exora. Its driver was uninjured," he said.
He said the case was being investigated under Sections 41(1) and 43(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.

Title: SAR for missing One Fathom Bank angler called off after six days
Article:
KLANG: The search and rescue (SAR) operation for anglers reported missing at One Fathom Bank near Pulau Ketam since last Monday was called off today after no new leads or discoveries were reported.
Selangor Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) operations officer Lieutenant Mohd Azlee Zainal said the six-day operation covered a radius of 3,887 square nautical miles in the waters of Selangor and Perak.
"The operation until 7pm last night did not find any new leads or the one angler who is still
missing.
"Consequently, the SAR operation covering the sea and air sectors, including the waters of Hutan Melintang and Bagan Datuk, is terminated," he told Bernama at the Forward Search and Rescue Base (PHC) at Sementa Jetty here last night.
Earlier, he briefed dozens of family members waiting for updates on the operation at the PHC.
Azlee said although the SAR operation had been terminated, MMEA assets would continue routine patrols and monitoring in the waters.
"We have also informed the fishermen's association and the maritime community to cooperate if they have new information or make any discoveries regarding the missing angler. Any information can be channelled directly to the MMEA or police for further action," he said.
The SAR operation involved assets including maritime vessels KM Nusa and KM Tugau, a CL415MP aircraft and an RH33 patrol boat from the Marine Police Force (PPM).
Last Monday, Selangor MMEA launched the SAR operation after receiving an official report at 3.35am on the disappearance of seven anglers at One Fathom Bank.
Four of the anglers were found safe, while two died. Muhammad Ridzuan Ruhaizat, 37, and Mohamad Shahril Abd Rahman, 43, were found in the waters off Hutan Melintang last Wednesday and Thursday respectively.
Meanwhile, Khairul Muhidin, 47, the uncle of Muhammad Ridzuan, said his nephew's remains were buried at the Jalan Kebun Barat Muslim Cemetery in Shah Alam at 5.15pm today.
He said the funeral prayer for the deceased, whose remains were claimed by the family from Sungai Buloh Hospital this afternoon, was held at the An-Naim Mosque in Jalan Kebun at 4.30pm.
"We accept Allah's will and are thankful that all the funeral arrangements went smoothly, including the deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) testing process by the hospital," he said.
Another missing angler, Raja Mohd Rozi Raja Mahamud, 49, has yet to be found.

Title: 'Here's how to write it': Akmal dares Nga to honour resignation pledge after Loke quits
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh has reminded Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming of his earlier pledge to resign, following DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke's announcement that he was stepping down as transport minister.
In a Facebook post, Akmal said Loke's resignation was a case of "ordering one thing and getting another".
"If you have forgotten or are pretending to forget, let me remind you how to write a resignation letter.
"You can share it with your other friends too, if they dare," he said.
Earlier,
Loke announced his resignation
as transport minister following the decision to grant former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak conditional house arrest.
However, Loke said other DAP ministers and deputy ministers would remain in the Unity Government.
He also acknowledged that some quarters were waiting for DAP to leave the government so Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim would lose parliamentary support, potentially leading to the dissolution of Parliament.
Nga, who is also DAP deputy chairman, had previously said he would be the
first minister to resign
if Umno won a landslide victory in the Johor election and Najib was released without serving a fitting sentence.
Meanwhile, Akmal also shared a July 12 post featuring his resignation letter as a Melaka executive councillor, offering it as a reference for Nga.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fahmi says misleading online health ad complaints will be sent to MCMC for review
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — Complaints about online health advertisements and promotions that may violate regulations and mislead the public will be referred to the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC).
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the matter was among the issues raised during his meeting with representatives from medical associations and healthcare experts in Kuala Lumpur today.
“The matter will be referred to MCMC for review and further action with the relevant parties,” he said in a Facebook post.
He said the meeting was held to hear the views, suggestions and concerns raised by the representatives and medical experts.
Fahmi also expressed appreciation for the open and constructive discussions, saying insights from those directly involved were important to help understand the actual issues and find more effective solutions. — Bernama

Title: Haze watch: 21 areas nationwide wake up to unhealthy air
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — Haze continued to cloud parts of the country this morning, with 21 areas recording unhealthy air quality as of 8am.
Sarawak recorded the highest readings, led by the Serian district police headquarters at 182 on the Air Pollutant Index (API), followed by Samarahan at 168 and Sri Aman at 164, according to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System.
Johor also saw unhealthy air quality in Larkin, which recorded 162, and Pasir Gudang at 155.
Putrajaya, Nilai in Negeri Sembilan and Batu Pahat in Johor each recorded an API reading of 154.
In Selangor, Shah Alam recorded 153 while Johan Setia registered 127, while Cheras was the only area in Kuala Lumpur in the unhealthy category, with a reading of 133.
Another 41 areas recorded moderate air quality, including Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur and Miri in Sarawak, both at 99, and Politeknik Kota Kinabalu at 98.
Five areas recorded good air quality, with Tanah Merah in Kelantan registering 47, Sungai Petani in Kedah 41 and Alor Setar 35.
Under the API classification, readings of 0 to 50 indicate good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy and 301 and above hazardous.

Title: Sabah tourism bucks the slump talk with 4.1pc rise
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 20 — Sabah tourist arrivals rose 4.1 per cent from January to August, disproving talk of a slump in the state’s tourism sector.
State Tourism, Culture and Environment Assistant Minister Dr Andi Md Shamsureezal Mohd Sainal said there had been an increase in both international and domestic arrivals during the period.
“The talk that Sabah’s tourism is declining is not true at all,” he said after officiating the opening ceremony of the Malaysian Association of Tour and Travel Agents (Matta) Fair Sabah at the Sabah International Convention Centre, here, Saturday.
“From January to August this year, tourist numbers increased 4.1 per cent. International arrivals rose about 6.9 per cent, while local Malaysian visitors grew 2.1 per cent compared with last year,” he said.
For the record, this is the second Matta Fair held in Sabah this year, following the first edition in April.
“This time, we brought in travel agents to offer very attractive packages to draw more tourists to Sabah,” he said.
“On behalf of the State Government, I greatly appreciate and support initiatives like this by Matta to increase tourist arrivals and to promote Sabah to the world,” he added.
Asked whether the fair was part of preparations for Visit Sabah 2027, Dr Andi said it was.
“Certainly, Matta Fair is one of the programmes we have planned. God willing, in November we will release the full calendar for Visit Sabah 2027,” he said.
He said Sabah was also being actively promoted overseas, pointing out that State Tourism, Culture and Environment Minister Datuk Jafry Ariffin was currently in China to promote the state’s tourism sector.
The three-day fair is being held until today (Sunday) and is open to the public from 10am to 9pm.
It features 83 booths involving 28 tour and travel agencies, three hotels and resorts, two state tourism offices and four other travel-related service providers.
For the record, the April edition attracted an estimated 37,499 visitors and generated about RM24 million in sales.
For this edition, the Matta Sabah Chapter has set a target of 30,000 visitors and RM28 million in sales.
The fair is endorsed by the Sabah Tourism Board, with RHB Bank as the bank partner and Malaysia Aviation Group as the official airline partner and premier sponsor. Tourism Johor is also taking part.
Matta Sabah Chapter Chairman Alex Chong said the fair was more than a platform for selling holiday packages.
“It connects travellers with professional travel agents and tourism businesses while creating opportunities across the wider tourism ecosystem,” he said.
He said this year’s theme, “Discover More. Travel More. Experience More”, reflected the association’s encouragement for Sabahans to explore destinations in Sabah, Malaysia and overseas.
“At the same time, we are promoting Sabah as a destination for domestic and international travellers,” he said.
Present were Matta president Nigel Wong, among others. — Daily Express

Title: Fire Dept: SAR launched after hiker slips down slope and becomes separated from group in Gua Musang
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Sept 20 — The Kelantan Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) launched a search and rescue (SAR) operation last night for a male hiker who became separated from his group in the jungle near Kem Tudung Periuk, Gua Musang.
The victim, Muhammad Asrul Quyyum Asmmuddin, 23, is believed to have slipped from the hiking trail and fallen down a slope. He did not sustain serious injuries and is able to walk.
A Kelantan JBPM spokesman said the Operations Control Centre (PGO) contacted the victim, despite unstable phone coverage in the area, and he shared his location through WhatsApp.
“The victim has a torchlight, a whistle, and about 75 per cent battery life remaining on his smartphone.
“He has been instructed to stay at his current location while waiting for the SAR team to arrive, as well as to conserve his phone battery and torch light,” he said in a statement last night.
He said the victim was advised to blow his whistle three times at intervals of a few minutes, then stop and listen for a response.
“If he hears a whistle or voices, the victim is asked to first determine the direction of the sound rather than moving towards it immediately.
“The victim was also requested to inform Kelantan PGO if he is found by any SAR team,” he said, adding that the operation is still ongoing.
JBPM received a call about the incident at 8.08pm. The Gua Musang Fire and Rescue Station sent a Fire Rescue Tender and a Hilux vehicle to the location, 116 kilometres from the station. — Bernama

Title: Santap Lah: Ready-to-eat meals from Malaysia’s Michelin selected restaurants at a CAFé by 7-Eleven near you
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 20 — What if having a restaurant-quality meal is possible with just the press of a button?
This is what sparked the birth of Santap Lah, a newly launched brand of microwaveable meals curated, prepared and approved by chefs from Michelin recognised restaurants in Malaysia.
Benson Chang used to grab a quick lunch from the convenience store near his office on busy days but one day, while having his usual microwaved meal, he wondered if he could work with some restaurants to produce better quality ready-to-eat meals.
That was the spark that led the Santap Lah managing director to seek out chefs from restaurants that he was familiar with.
Chang, who is the founder of restaurant reservation platform TableApp, is no stranger to many restaurants and chefs in Malaysia.
“I was close with many chefs so when I got this idea, I started asking my chef friends if they were interested in developing this with me,” he said in a recent interview with
Malay Mail.
His idea was to produce good quality, delicious and ready-to-eat meals that have a shelf life of at least a year without being frozen or refrigerated.
“After asking around, several chefs showed interest and that was when we started developing recipes for the meals,” he said.
Chang also has a contact who operated a retort food manufacturing facility to produce and pack the meals.
“It took two years of development, testing the recipes over and over, going back and forth with the chefs to make sure the flavours and textures are up to standard,” he said.
The manufacturing process of the meals uses high temperature and pressure to sterilise the food, allowing the sealed meals to be stored at room temperature without refrigeration.
“We also sent the meals to be tested in laboratories and results placed their shelf life at up to 18 months, but we opted to place a 12-month expiry period on the meals to be safe,” he said.
The products are manufactured in a halal-certified facility using halal-certified ingredients and contain no added preservatives or MSG.
“Being chefs from Michelin-selected restaurants, they are of course quite particular about ingredients being used, they absolutely do not want any artificial flavourings, preservatives or MSG,” he said.
Selecting the type of meals was also a challenge due to the manufacturing and packing process as it would mean they cannot have crispy components, vegetables or most seafood.
“Crispy food will just become soggy in the process, the vegetables will oxidise and change colour while seafood does not respond well to prolonged heat,” he said.
He said this was why they had to only work with braised, steamed and oven-cooked dishes using chicken, beef, lamb, mushrooms and other vegetarian ingredients.
He said each time the meal was produced, the chef would rate the flavours.
“The first time the food came out, the quality was already very good as the chefs gave it about 6.5 or seven out of 10,” Chang said.
They subsequently suggested adjustments to the texture, colour, seasoning and water content of each dish.
“The samples went through several trial runs until the chefs gave scores of at least 8.5 before we started mass production and distribution,” he said.
However, Chang said every production batch is still sent to the respective chef for quality control, while some of them also buy the products from 7-Eleven outlets to check their consistency.
“The main focus of Santap Lah is on Malaysian flavours, thus our tagline ‘Taste the Malaysian Story’,” he said.
In the first phase of volume one of Santap Lah: Taste the Malaysian Story are four rice meals from Restaurant au Jardin’s Kim Hock Su, akar’s Aidan Low, Beta KL’s Raymond Tham and Jawi House’s Nurilkarim Razha.
The four rice dishes introduced are Kim Hock’s hericium mushroom
rendang
with rose water rice, Aidan’s
dabai
curry rice, Raymond’s
kadok
chicken rice and Nurilkarim’s rose chicken with buttered rice.
Chang said they will be releasing the noodle-based meals next month by Dewakan’s Darren Teoh, Gai’s Darren Chin, and gēn根’s Johnson Wong.
The noodle dishes are Teoh’s Dewakan
laksa,
Chin’s
tom yam
ramen and Wong’s
buah kulim
noodle.
The rice dishes are priced at RM15.90 each, while the noodle meals cost RM19.90.
The four rice meals are now available at selected CAFé by 7-Eleven outlets nationwide. — Picture by Opalyn Mok
The food of Penang celebrations
One of the chefs, Nurilkarim, said Santap Lah offers him another avenue to introduce Jawi Peranakan and local Malay cooking to a wider audience.
His rose chicken with buttered rice, or
nasi minyak
and
ayam ros
, is inspired from a Jawi House signature and a recipe published in his mother’s cookbook,
Feast of Penang.
The chicken is prepared in a creamy tomato-and-onion gravy containing cashew nuts, candlenuts, spices and chilli before being finished with rose water.
“Penang-style
ayam ros
is different from the
ayam masak merah
commonly served at
kenduri
elsewhere,” he said.
He added that
nasi minyak i
s traditionally associated with weddings,
doa selamat
ceremonies and other celebrations.
“When people see a couple getting serious, the elderly will say, ‘
Boleh bau dah nasi minyak
’, they can already smell the
nasi minyak
brewing which means a
kenduri
is on the way,” he said.
He said this was why he chose to pair the
